current.title: Your City Is Secretly 8 Degrees Hotter Than It Should Be
current.hook: The city itself is cooking your block.
current.closing: The redlining maps are gone. The heat still remembers them.
current.question: Does your neighborhood feel hotter than it should? Tell me below.

segments.say: Across 65 major US cities, pavement and buildings add an average of 8 degrees of extra heat. New York adds 9.7, San Francisco 9.1 -- heat with no clouds involved, just concrete.

segments.topic: who lives in the hotter city blocks
segments.say: That heat isn't spread evenly. 68 percent of everyone studied live in the very hottest pockets -- older, paved-over blocks with almost no tree cover left.

segments.topic: why some neighborhoods got hotter first
segments.say: This isn't random. Neighborhoods redlined back in the 1930s are, on average, 5 degrees hotter today than nearby areas that weren't -- sometimes over 12. The maps are gone. The heat still follows them.

judge.one_line: Mostly charts with the mascot parked on them, plus colliding and low-contrast labels (seg1:end, seg2:start, seg4). The redlining reveal, the story's core, is a two-bar chart with a '0' baseline.
problems: Hook (hook@0.3 to hook@2.2): a static bubble ranking under a plain title, with no immediate action or reason to stay.
seg0: the NYC value '9.7' looks smeared or overprinted, and Data just stands on the bubble.
seg2:start: the 32% label is grey-on-grey and nearly invisible, and the header is truncated with an ellipsis.
seg3: the core redlining claim is a bar vs a '0' stub in a mostly empty frame, and 'sometimes over 12' is never shown.
seg4: the speech-bubble tail slices through the 'Formerly redlined neighborhoods' label, and Data covers several thermometers.
fixes: Open on motion: a city block heating up and Data reacting (fanning himself, pavement shimmering), not a bubble layout.
Show the redline effect spatially: an old HOLC map boundary over a block map where the redlined side glows 5 degrees hotter and flares to 12.
Replace the stacked column in seg2 with 100 people or blocks, 68 of them turning red-hot.
Separate the seg1 annotation from the '65-city average 8' label, and move the seg4 bubble tail off the heading.
Give text labels in seg2 full-contrast ink, and shorten the headers so they aren't truncated.
Keep Data off the numbers and marks he currently covers (the NYC 9.7 bubble, the seg4 thermometers).

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.
Each SAY is one spoken sentence or two, at most 40 words, and says its beat's headline number out loud.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'. Write answer_path as one JSON object matching answer_schema, request_id and slug copied, and commit it. Do not touch the request.
